facts.text: Publish throws invalid_out when the Out option is null or whitespace.
Publish throws invalid_format unless Format is md or jsonl.
With jsonl format Publish raises invalid_assets unless Assets is embed, files or none.
In jsonl format a negative MaxFiles, MaxFileBytes or MaxTotalBytes raises invalid_limit.
at: max-files, max-file-bytes and max-total-bytes must be zero (unlimited) or greater

facts.text: In markdown format Publish raises invalid_depth when Depth is not index or full.
In markdown format Publish raises invalid_facts when Facts is not detail or none.
In markdown format a negative Budget raises invalid_budget.
at: budget must be zero or greater

facts.text: In markdown format Publish raises invalid_index_max_tokens when IndexMaxTokens is below 1.
Setting RespectLimits without a ProfilePath raises invalid_profile.
Publish loads the profile before opening the store or the output directory, so a bad profile file fails first.
at: Load the profile before touching the store or the output directory

facts.text: A subject with no live fact and no descendant holding one gets no bundle directory.
at: A subject with no live fact and no descendant holding one

facts.text: Ancestors of a kept subject stay in the bundle even with no fact of their own, and the scope root always stays.
at: the tree runs through them, and the scope root always stays

facts.text: Publish loads slot occupants from the slots table ordered by kind then fact_id.
at: SELECT subject_id, key, fact_id FROM slots ORDER BY kind, fact_id

facts.text: Shard mode writes no fact files and no assets because each shard is a self-contained document.
at: Shard mode writes no fact files and no assets: a shard is a self-contained document.

facts.text: Facts are ordered by subject tree position first, then key, kind, text, ContentHash and id.
A missing attachment blob adds a warning naming the sha256 and the subject, and the publish continues.
The compliance report measures every generated file and asset but excludes the bundle manifest.
In shard mode only files under shards/ are measured and manifest.json is named a navigation aid.
at: are navigation aids and not counted

facts.text: The bundle hash is computed while README.md still holds its generated-at placeholder.
When the previous manifest hash matches the new one, Publish reuses the stored timestamp instead of reading the clock.
README.md records the supplied CommandLine, or a command line synthesized from the options when it is null.
Each subject page is compiled with OmitStatusNotes set, so it prints the stored status and is charged for plain lines.
In markdown detail mode an attachment whose sha256 fails the hex pattern is treated as missing.
When the attachment file exists, the published byte count comes from the file on disk rather than the stored record.
Subject directory slugs are capped at 80 characters.
Fact file name stems are capped at 48 characters.
Bundle keys start as the first 8 hex characters of the digest.
LegacyAssetPathRegex matches the old assets directory layout so a republish can still clean those files up.
README.md is first built with the TimestampPlaceholder text so the README does not affect the bundle hash.
Publish rewrites a generated file only when its bytes change.
at: only rewritten when their bytes change

facts.text: Attachment file name stems are capped at 40 characters.
Sha256Hex matches a lowercase 64-character hex blob hash.
The generated AGENTS.md receives the detail flag, IndexMaxTokens and the shard flag.
AssetPathRegex matches subjects/<slug>/assets/<name>.<ext> paths used to classify generated files.
A published attachment whose blob is missing or not linked has no assets file written for it.
at: An attachment as published: Name is the file under subjects/

facts.text: Assets defaults to files in jsonl format and to detail in markdown format.
Budget defaults to DossierStore.DefaultBudgetTokens.
Format defaults to the md constant.
at: public string Format { get; set; } = FormatMarkdown;

facts.text: PublishOptions.Depth defaults to full.
PublishOptions.Facts defaults to detail, which writes one file per fact.
LoadPubSubjects reads subjects with the id, name, kind, parent_id, aliases and pin columns, ordered by id.
at: SELECT id, name, kind, parent_id, aliases, pin FROM subjects ORDER BY id

facts.text: A subject row whose parent_id is NULL becomes a PubSubject with a null ParentId.
LoadPubFacts skips facts whose status is superseded or retracted and facts of kind dossier.
at: WHERE status NOT IN ('superseded', 'retracted') AND kind <> 'dossier'

facts.text: Facts whose subject is outside the selected set are skipped rather than filtered in SQL.
After reading the fact rows, LoadPubFacts loads each fact's refs and attachments by fact id.
SubtreeOf walks parent links breadth first from the root id and returns the root plus every descendant found.
TreeOrder treats a subject as a root when it has no ParentId or its parent is not in the loaded set.
TreeOrder builds each subject's display path by joining ancestor names with a slash surrounded by spaces.
Siblings are sorted by normalized name, then name, kind, joined aliases and id.
SlugCore keeps only lowercase ASCII letters and digits, collapsing each run of other characters into one hyphen.
When a slug exceeds the maximum, SlugCore truncates it and trims trailing hyphens.
Slugify returns subject when a name produces an empty slug.
AssignSlugs gives colliding subjects the base slug for the first in tree order and -2, -3 for the rest.
at: the first keeps the base slug

facts.text: AssignSlugs increments the numeric suffix until it finds a slug not already taken.
DefaultBundleHash returns the lowercase hex SHA-256 digest of the key input.
BundleKeyInput joins normalized text, key, kind and canonical data with unit separators.
WriteCanonicalJson writes object properties in ordinal order of their names.
PublishResult.Warnings holds one line per missing blob and the bundle is still written.
at: fail-open: the bundle is still written

facts.text: PublishResult.Assets counts distinct asset records and is set only for jsonl output.
at: the number of distinct asset records written
